```{r Reading Data}
library(tidyverse)

data <- read_csv("../data/cleaned_combined_data.csv")
```

```{r Cleaning data}
course_data <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(c(1:4, 24:41))

course_data_long <- course_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(5:22),
    names_to = "courses",
    values_to = "taken"
  )

course_means <- course_data_long %>% 
  group_by(courses, taken) %>% 
  summarise(
    mean_prog = mean(prog.comf),
    mean_math = mean(math.comf),
    mean_stat = mean(stat.comf),
    count = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

course_means_grouped <- course_means %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = courses,                              
    names_from = taken,                             
    values_from = c(mean_prog, mean_math, mean_stat, count), 
    names_glue = "{.value}_{ifelse(taken, 'taken', 'not_taken')}"
  )
```


```{r Comparing mean comfort scores of those who have taken the class against those who have not, fig.show='hold', out.width="50%"}
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
#Programming Comparison
ggplot(course_means_grouped) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = courses, xend = courses, y = mean_prog_not_taken, yend = mean_prog_taken), color = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_prog_not_taken, color = "Not Taken"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_prog_taken, color = "Taken"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Course Status", values = c("Taken" = "#33B31A80", "Not Taken" = "#B3331A80")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Course Code", y = "Mean Programming Comfort Level")

#Math Comparison
ggplot(course_means_grouped) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = courses, xend = courses, y = mean_math_not_taken, yend = mean_math_taken), color = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_math_not_taken, color = "Not Taken"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_math_taken, color = "Taken"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Course Status", values = c("Taken" = "#33B31A80", "Not Taken" = "#B3331A80")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Course Code", y = "Mean Mathematics Comfort Level")

#Stats Comparison
ggplot(course_means_grouped) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = courses, xend = courses, y = mean_stat_not_taken, yend = mean_stat_taken), color = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_stat_not_taken, color = "Not Taken"), size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = courses, y = mean_stat_taken, color = "Taken"), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Course Status", values = c("Taken" = "#33B31A80", "Not Taken" = "#B3331A80")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Course Code", y = "Mean Statistics Comfort Level")

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```

Before running any regression, we must analyze the correlation between classes to see if dimension reduction is necessary.

```{r Plotting Correlation}
library(corrplot) #For using corrplot

class_cor <- cor(course_data %>% dplyr::select(-response_id, -prog.comf, -math.comf, -stat.comf)) 
#%>% 
 # corr.test(method = "pearson", adjust = "BY")
corrplot(class_cor, method = "square", type = "full", order = "hclust", addCoef.col = "black", number.cex = 0.5)
```
There's no significant correlation besides cases of extremely small sample size, such as the one student taking both Linguistic classes or the one student who hasn't taken PSTAT 126, and a negative correlation between CS9 and CS16, which are mutually exclusive classes in terms of requirements for the PSTAT preparation for the major. I tried fitting all sorts of regressions to the data, but none were particularly effective, so I've decided to fit a random forest instead:

```{r Fitting Random Forests}
library(randomForest)
library(ordinalForest)
set.seed(10152026)

course_data_numeric <- course_data %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.integer)) %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub(" ", "_", .x), everything()) %>% 
  mutate(prog.comf = factor(prog.comf, levels = 2:5, ordered = TRUE),
         math.comf = factor(math.comf, levels = 2:5, ordered = TRUE),
         stat.comf = factor(stat.comf, levels = 3:5, ordered = TRUE))

prog_rf_data <- course_data_numeric %>%
  dplyr::select(-response_id, -math.comf, -stat.comf)
math_rf_data <- course_data_numeric %>%
  dplyr::select(-response_id, -prog.comf, -stat.comf)
stat_rf_data <- course_data_numeric %>%
  dplyr::select(-response_id, -math.comf, -prog.comf)

prog_rf <- randomForest(prog.comf ~ ., data = prog_rf_data, ntree = 500, mtry = 4, importance = TRUE)
math_rf <- randomForest(math.comf ~ ., data = math_rf_data, ntree = 500, mtry = 4, importance = TRUE)
stat_rf <- randomForest(stat.comf ~ ., data = stat_rf_data, ntree = 500, mtry = 4, importance = TRUE)
```

```{r Plotting the Random Forests, fig.show='hold', out.width="50%"}
library(knitr)
#Used DeepSeek to make the Kable
get_imp <- function(model, label) {
  as.data.frame(randomForest::importance(model)) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("class") %>%
    transmute(class, importance = MeanDecreaseAccuracy, outcome = label)
}

imp_table <- bind_rows(
  get_imp(prog_rf, "Programming"),
  get_imp(math_rf, "Math"),
  get_imp(stat_rf, "Statistics")
) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = importance) %>%
  arrange(desc(Programming)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))

knitr::kable(imp_table, 
      caption = "Mean Decrease in Accuracy by class and comfort type",
      col.names = c("Class", "Programming", "Math", "Statistics"))
varImpPlot(prog_rf)
varImpPlot(math_rf)
varImpPlot(stat_rf)
```
